scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: A vague note
scenes.caption: Reva opens a pretend fair lending desk. Nikhil brings a note asking for a small kit for each group. Before sorting paper tools, they ask what small means and what the desk should produce.
scenes.speech: Reva opens a pretend fair lending desk. Nikhil brings a note asking for a small kit for each group. Before sorting paper tools, they ask what small means and what the desk should produce.
scenes.dialogue: Could two volunteers pack different kits?

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: Name the inputs
scenes.caption: The supplied list names each group and its requested tool counts. These are inputs, not promises about the result. Reva proposes an output card showing the packed counts and whether the request fits the available carrying box.
scenes.speech: The supplied list names each group and its requested tool counts. These are inputs, not promises about the result. Reva proposes an output card showing the packed counts and whether the request fits the available carrying box.
scenes.dialogue: An input starts the work; an output records it.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: A measurable limit
scenes.caption: Their fictional box holds at most eight space tokens. Each paper clamp uses two tokens and each ruler uses one. A request for three clamps and two rulers fills the box exactly, so equality must count as fitting.
scenes.speech: Their fictional box holds at most eight space tokens. Each paper clamp uses two tokens and each ruler uses one. A request for three clamps and two rulers fills the box exactly, so equality must count as fitting.
scenes.dialogue: Write the unit beside the limit.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Resolve the disagreement
scenes.caption: Nikhil suggests accepting anything that looks light. Reva wants the same token calculation for every request. Choose a specification that different volunteers can apply consistently, including a clear response when a request exceeds the box limit.
scenes.speech: Nikhil suggests accepting anything that looks light. Reva wants the same token calculation for every request. Choose a specification that different volunteers can apply consistently, including a clear response when a request exceeds the box limit.
scenes.dialogue: A rule needs an observable result.

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Tests reveal meanings
scenes.caption: They try an empty request, a box filled exactly and an oversized request. Those cases separate possible interpretations of small. An empty kit is allowed in this simulation; negative counts are outside the accepted input rules and need correction.
scenes.speech: They try an empty request, a box filled exactly and an oversized request. Those cases separate possible interpretations of small. An empty kit is allowed in this simulation; negative counts are outside the accepted input rules and need correction.
scenes.dialogue: Record the expected response before checking.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: A specification card
scenes.caption: Their final card names the inputs, token formula, inclusive limit and possible outputs. Another volunteer can check new requests without guessing the writer’s intention. Keep passing and failing examples beside it.
scenes.speech: Their final card names the inputs, token formula, inclusive limit and possible outputs. Another volunteer can check new requests without guessing the writer’s intention. Keep passing and failing examples beside it.
scenes.dialogue: Can someone else repeat your test?
